entry.title: SFST moves Second Reading of Securities and Futures (Amendment) Bill 2026
entry.summary: FSTB moved Second Reading of the Bill, which proposes REIT restructuring and compulsory-acquisition mechanisms and extends aspects of market-misconduct and disclosure regulation to listed collective investment schemes. It remains subject to passage; certain disclosure amendments are expected on 4 December 2027.

entry.title: LCQ14: Building international gold trading market
entry.summary: The government reported that the gold clearing and settlement system is in trial operation with 11 provisional direct-participant banks and is planned to launch in Q1 2027. It is to connect with RTGS for delivery-versus-payment before launch; no bank participation requirement or compliance deadline is stated.

entry.title: Northern Metropolis Financial Advisory Taskforce holds its third meeting
entry.summary: HKMA proposes amending the Banking (Capital) Rules to designate specified government-related entities as Domestic Public Sector Entities to support financing for Northern Metropolis projects. The proposal is not enacted; HKMA intends to submit amendments to Legislative Council in Q1 2027, with a view to effect in Q2 2027.

entry.title: Amendments to HKSCC Rules, Operational Procedures and FINI Terms and Conditions
entry.summary: HKSCC states that the SFC approved amendments to its rules, procedures and FINI terms for the Uncertificated Securities Market initiative. The amendments take effect on 16 November 2026 and include defined participant controls for uncertificated securities transfers and ASR-fee arrangements.

entry.title: Government welcomes passage of Inland Revenue (Amendment) (Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework and Amended Common Reporting Standard) Bill 2026
entry.summary: The Government announced that the Legislative Council passed the Bill to implement OECD CARF and amended CRS. Relevant service providers will collect CARF-specified information in 2027 for IRD exchanges from 2028; amended CRS takes effect in 2028 and exchanges begin in 2029. IRD will issue guidance and provide technical support.

entry.title: LCQ1: Policy on the development of digital assets
entry.summary: In a Legislative Council reply, the Government said it and the SFC will introduce a Bill by end-2026 to extend the virtual-asset regime to dealing, advisory, management and custody. FSTB and HKMA are advancing a legislative review on wider distributed-ledger-technology use in fixed income and digital assets. The reply is a policy statement and future legislative intention, not an enacted rule.

entry.title: Future of Finance Institute Commences Operations, Starting with AI in Finance
entry.summary: MAS announced that Singapore's Future of Finance Institute has commenced operations. Its initial AI work includes good practices and practical resources for AI use-case risk assessment, testing and assurance, and third-party AI; the release describes an industry initiative rather than a new binding instrument.

entry.title: Supplemental circular to management companies of SFC-authorised funds on liquidity risk management
entry.summary: The SFC circular sets enhanced liquidity-risk-management guidance for managers of SFC-authorised open-ended funds, including expectations on liquidity assessment, liquidity-management tools, investor disclosure and reporting when specified tools or measures are activated.

entry.title: SFC issues guidance to support enhancements to Hong Kong’s retail fund regime
entry.summary: The SFC announced guidance, FAQs, updated application guides and key facts statement templates to support the revised UT Code, covering derivatives exposure, liquidity risk, money market funds, disclosures and transition arrangements.

entry.title: SFC approves first-ever secondary trading of tokenised public funds
entry.summary: The SFC approved secondary trading of two existing SFC-authorised tokenised money-market funds on an SFC-licensed virtual-asset trading platform, with around-the-clock trading beginning on 26 October 2026. The approval applies the April 2026 pilot framework; it is not a new sector-wide rule or direct instruction outside the approved arrangement.

entry.title: HSBC launches new AI-enabled solution to transform transaction banking
entry.summary: HSBC announced HSBCnio for corporate and institutional clients, with existing-permission web/mobile access, APIs and read-only access by client AI tools to authorised account and transaction data. This is a bank product announcement and a commercial/control benchmark, not a Hong Kong regulatory change or sector-wide obligation.

entry.title: HSBC RedCoin launches today
entry.summary: HSBC states that its HKD-denominated RedCoin became available on PayMe on 23 October 2026. It says users will be able to activate wallets for peer-to-peer and merchant payments, with later-2026 plans for mobile-app wallets, tokenised-investment subscriptions and wholesale use cases.

entry.title: Canada Gazette, Part I, Volume 160, Number 43: Stablecoin Regulations
entry.summary: Canada’s Department of Finance prepublished proposed Stablecoin Regulations on 24 October 2026, with related Retail Payment Activities Regulations amendments. The consultation proposes requirements for issuer registration, reserves, redemption, governance, data security, recovery and resolution, reporting and notices; representations are invited within 60 days.

entry.title: Gazettal of revised SPM module CA-B-2 “Systemically Important Banks”
entry.summary: HKMA gazetted CA-B-2 V.3 effective 23 October 2026, replacing V.2. The revised D-SIB assessment adds RTGS/FPS turnover to deposits and customer lending as substitutability indicators; all licensed banks are in the regular assessment scope and other authorised institutions may be included case by case.

entry.title: Anti-bribery & corruption controls for account opening
entry.summary: HKMA issued a circular to all authorised institutions on account-opening bribery risks. It expects layered, risk-based onboarding and proportionate customer due diligence, with segregation of duties and enhanced controls for third-party introducer cases; no source deadline is stated.

entry.title: HSBC RedCoin launches today
entry.summary: HSBC says its HKD stablecoin, RedCoin (RCHKD), will be available from launch on PayMe. In the coming days, the bank says more than 3.3 million PayMe users will be able to activate an in-app wallet and use it for peer-to-peer and peer-to-merchant payments, including at more than 100,000 merchants; it also describes later planned mobile-app, tokenised-investment and wholesale use cases.

entry.title: Anti-bribery & corruption controls for account opening
entry.summary: HKMA issued a current circular to all Authorized Institutions on bribery and corruption risks in account opening. It expects a layered, risk-based approach and proportionate customer due diligence; segregation of duties and enhanced controls for third-party agents are explicit requirements. No source deadline is stated.

entry.title: LCQ1: Improving online bank account opening
entry.summary: A Legislative Council reply reports existing HKMA expectations for remote account-opening identity verification, control enhancement, ongoing due diligence, transaction monitoring and suspicious-transaction reporting. It also reports first-phase iAM Smart step-up-authentication testing; any expansion remains subject to HKMA’s assessment of security, stability and customer experience on a risk-based approach.

entry.title: Building the future of finance in the age of AI
entry.summary: In a drafted speech, the Financial Conduct Authority shared AI good and poor practice drawn from firm testing, covering customer escalation, governance, testing, monitoring, resilience and supplier dependencies. The FCA said significant AI failures and near misses should be covered by UK major-incident reporting and said it will develop an agentic-finance framework. This is a UK speech and an analogous control benchmark, not a Hong Kong obligation.

entry.title: Implementation of T+1 Settlement Cycle for Hong Kong Cash Market
entry.summary: HKSCC states that, subject to market readiness and regulatory approval, Hong Kong cash-market settlement will move from T+2 to T+1 in the second half of 2028. The circular asks Clearing Participants to assess T-day post-trade operations, liquidity and funding, client cut-offs and communications, customer documents, and exception controls.
